summary:
# NOTES: *Viennese Medley* (Edith O'Shaughnessy, 1924; Vienna, post-war hunger years 1919-21)
Dedicated to Countesses Miton and Gladys Széchényi. Epigraph: "'S giebt nur a Kaiserstadt, 'S giebt nur a Wien." Seven chapters, each with a music tempo marking and an epigraph.

## Cast
- **Frau Ildefonse "Tante Ilde" Stacher, née von Berg**: ~70. Widow of Kommerzienrath Stacher (30 yrs Finance Ministry). Pale blue wide eyes, lace shawl, gold chain, gold watch, gold bracelets (baby teeth marks), amethyst-pearl ring. Corinne calls her "my Dresden china Auntie." Lost Bohemian beet-root shares (dowry) when Czecho-Slovakia formed. Childless. Lived at Baden house.
- **Heinie (Heinrich Bruckner)**: her brother, Northern Railways official, dead 7 yrs. Married 3 times. 11 children plus adopted Jella. Third wife **Irma Milanovics** (Croatian, Plitvicer Lakes/Agram).
- **Irma**: sour, fierce, petit-point embroiderer, failing eyes, red three-cornered shawl, "Business is business," hoards food. Lives Hoher Markt area, 5 flights up.
- **Irma's sons**: **Ferry** (eldest, thin, cough, whittles wooden peasant woman with two buckets), **Gusl** (hungry), **little Heinie**.
- **Corinne**: best-loved niece, half-sister of Kaethe, tall, blond, blue eyes, "oblique look," works at Depositen Bank (zeros, billions). Pauli loves her.
- **Liesel**: Heinie's daughter. Married ~2 yrs to **Otto Steiner** (Ministry of Agriculture, accountant, limp from knee, frozen toes lost in Italian camp, pince-nez, jealous "little Turk," Trabuco cigars, flute). Liesel plump, dimples, pink apron, makes noodles in butter.
- **Anna**: eldest niece, married to **Pauli Birbach**. Gaunt, dull, brooding, jealous of Fanny.
- **Hermine**: Anna's daughter, ugly, mirthless, named for Pauli's mother.
- **Pauli Birbach**: 40, handsome, Hungarian mother, Travel Bureau (Kärntnerring), zimbalon, luck in war, "lucky as Pauli Birbach." Gold ring with turquoise. Sisters widowed (Mimi); brother-in-law Geza killed on Galician hill ("I'm going up because I must"). Sisters' Groswardein lands lost to Romania.
- **Hermann Bruckner ("Manny")**: doctor, tall, black beard. Field hospital; right arm shattered at Gorizia; neurasthenia, agoraphobia (can't cross open spaces). Lost love **Marie von Sternberg**, Russian front, died of typhus after fever (Pripet marshes). Lost nerve at nosebleed. Sees Tante Ilde as only one to help him cross streets.
- **Mizzi (Maschka)**: Hermann's wife, 75 kg, lingerie shop in **Plankengasse**, Czech father Ottokar Maschka (dead). "Dumm, but dumm." Ruthless, admires profiteers, loves Fanny's money. Employees: **Tilly** (fairy fingers, dying mother), **Gretl** (servant).
- **Fanny**: Heinie's daughter, beautiful, sea-blue eyes, pale yellow hair, rich courtesan-like figure. Flat off Kaerntnerstrasse. Lunches at Hotel Bristol. Lover: a **Count** (cavalier, broke, South American girl wants him). Bought Mödling villa. Supports half the family. Blushes. Dresses in blue; black after Treaties.
- **Maria**: Fanny's old servant from father's house. Warm, shrewd, "weiss der Kuckuck," fortune-teller said "cattle" and a "letter."
- **Kaethe**: half-sister of Corinne, married **Professor Leo Eberhardt** (biology, Privatdozent-level, 'cello, now starving, bitter). Children: **Lilli** (~13, pansy eyes, pale gold hair, beautiful), **Resl** (dark, round, lucky), **Maxy**, **Hansi** (~6, dark curls), **Elsa**, **Carli** (~3, crystal face, legs can't hold him, dies), **Anny** (baby).
- **Marichi**: Koellner's daughter (~5-6), adopted by Eberhardts. Koellner (Privatdozent, violin, starving, consumptive wife dead).
- **Frau Kerzl**: landlady, son **Gusl** (TB, "Viennese malady"), spying, planned to replace Tante Ilde with an Englishman (pays shillings).
- **Others**: Dr Steier (Eberhardt's colleague, white hair), Frau Fuchs (fat, sable, Mercedes, banknotes), Schober (war-cripple dismissed), Amsel (composer, died), Rosetti (viola, lost).

## I. THEIR AUNT ILDE
- Pension gone. Baden house sold. Corinne breaks news. Tante Ilde weeps on Corinne's breast.
- Furniture sold; Tante Ilde boards at Frau Kerzl's (Spiegelgasse area, "Tante Dorothea's" = Dorotheum pawnshop).
- Dec: pawns gold bracelets at Dorotheum (weighed on scales; ticket). Jan: pawns watch, chain, amethyst-pearl ring.
- Jan 6 (Epiphany): Kerzl plans English lodger. Tante Ilde feels "one vast bruise."
- Corinne's weekly dinner plan: **Mon** Liesel; **Tue** Anna (Pauli arranged; meat day); **Wed** Mizzi (Fanny arranged); **Thu** Kaethe (bring whole dinner); **Fri** Corinne (place TBD); **Sat** TBD; **Sun** Irma (Corinne brings meat for boys' stew).
- Alcove at Irma's: brown plush divan from Baden, green-yellow chest, Haydn-leading-Mozart engraving, flat white-gilt vase, hook and eye on curtains. Corinne pays a month in advance.
- Tante Ilde: "I'm so grateful; I've had it hard." Corinne: "You've got to live."
- Last night at Kerzl's; "lived too long"; "no room of her own."

## II. LIESEL AND OTTO
- Leaves Kerzl's; Gusl coughing. Colonel-porter carries valises. "Courage," "auf Wiedersehen."
- Irma's alcove: Irma unwilling; chest of drawers forced in; nails in wall; drawers emptied except top. Irma: "I didn't think she had that much left." Corinne's "lilies of the field" and "pebbles hurt my feet" jokes lost on Irma. Irma's petit point (80,000 crowns medallion). Irma: "a plateful... she won't need the thick part."
- Tante Ilde dresses: black cloth suit with embroidered lapels, old lace collar, "Karlsbad" bar pin, black hat with faded purple knot.
- Liesel's flat: 3 rooms, Biedermeier furniture, green stove, mother's inlaid worktable. Noodles and fresh butter. Soup of black bread crusts. Veal cutlet for Otto. Voslauer wine. Toast "Prosit."
- Tante Ilde "does the dishes," cries to be allowed. Otto: "let Tante Ilde do as she will!"
- Stories: Liesel fell from Baden apple tree, broke wrist; races, Herr Hafner's 4-yr-old, Liesel won 20 Kronen. Fortune-teller: blond blue-eyed woman to avoid; dark-haired eyeglassed war-wounded man loves her.
- Liesel gives macaroni, brown sugar (for Irma), Otto's old shirts (for boys).
- Irma's supper: thin soup; Irma: "they're on their last legs." Boys do lessons under swinging lamp; Ferry whittles; Gusl hungry; little Heinie asleep. Irma wipes glasses. Irma's background: from Plitvicer Lakes; father's white house, chestnut tree, Milanovac Lake.
- Tante Ilde sleeps on brown divan. Hears Ferry cough.

## III. ANNA AND PAULI
- Mariahilferstrasse (drab, ugly). Anna's apartment: 3 sofas, dull cushions ("Nur ein viertel Stuendchen," "Traeume suess"), Dresden minuet figures (Pauli's gift), scarlet-clothed zimbalon, Hermine's cups "dem lieben Vater / der lieben Mutter."
- Pauli: "Anna? Dead since years. She ought to wear a bead wreath." Pauli loves Corinne since day at Kaethe's window waiting for rain.
- Tante Ilde walks Hoher Markt → Kärntnerstrasse (Zwieback window, Fanny's corner, Hotel Erzherzog Johann, Bristol, delicatessen, one-legged shoelace seller, Cambio/Devisen windows). Trolley fares too high.
- Dinner: potato soup, goulash, Palatschinken with ersatz jam; bottle of pale Tokay.
- Pauli kisses Tante Ilde: "Ach, the dear, lovely Auntie... Busserl." She: "Not lovely, only loving."
- Pauli: "In the Cafés, 3,000 crowns for bread..." Joke about cheese sleeve.
- Tante Ilde: "Corinne is an angel." Pauli: "She thinks you are one."
- Pauli plays wild Czardas, leaves abruptly. "It's understood, Tante Ilde, you're coming every Tuesday?"
- Tante Ilde thinks "poor Anna." Rain. "Why hadn't she walked in the morning?"

## IV. HERMANN AND MIZZI
- Hermann's war: joyful leaving for front; Gorizia bomb; arm ruined; neurasthenia; touches things twice; dwindling practice.
- Mizzi's shop success: Fanny's loan; Frau Fuchs; "Taktvoll kaschieren"; "Bustenhalter"; dessous; sells "Sachwerte." Dream of Carlsbad shop. Mizzi: "dumm, but dumm."
- Wed noon, Revolutionsplatz: Hermann at lamp-post. "Give me your arm." "All the good I do!" Hermann: "I thought I was going to heal the world."
- Dinner: lentil soup with ham-bone; herrings, potatoes; Apfelstrudel; real mocha. Mizzi: "Aren't you going to smoke?" Mizzi gives handkerchief with yellow stain.
- Mizzi's bag-sale of Irma's medallion (Archduchess story); Frau Fuchs pays in banknotes. Mizzi keeps Irma's money cut.
- Hermann's café thoughts: Tarok players, pikkolo; memory of Marie: Jan 1915 Elizabethspital, dying Tirolese youth "Mother"; Marie's blue eyes; Russian front; "Hermann, it is I"; typhus.
- Tante Ilde worries about Hermann, thinks of Fanny.

## V. THE EBERHARDTS
- Irma sees Frau Stacher shopping with string bag. Ferry's cough worse. Hermann: "he needs milk, eggs, high air." Suggests Fanny send him away. Irma: "Fanny, it's always Fanny."
- Eberhardt's apartment in Alsergrund near University. Past: "Jause," Kaethe's cakes, Schlagobers; children's milk jokes; Lilli's milky-way game. Kaethe played piano; Eberhardt 'cello. Amsel killed Eastern front; Koellner's Amati violin.
- Sarajevo 28 June; Emperor's griefs listed. War, Eberhardt's dysentery in delousing station.
- Shopping: Nestlé's milk taken by stout befurred woman who bids double (shopkeeper's "pig" joke). Small shriveled apples. Milk for Carli from grocer. Hard cheese, "feinste Keks" (12 biscuits, child-on-package picture). Rice (half kilo).
- Dinner at Kaethe's: rice with cheese; Carli sips "mimi" milk; Hansi caught with cheese rind ("whatever we have is for all of us"). Lilli returns with briquets (broken basket); Lilli in made-over sea-blue dress; Resl's luck (American woman, ten-shilling note, gold piece).
- Bread-line: Lilli queues at dawn (13 yrs). Friends package (lard, sugar, flour, cocoa, coffee).
- Lilli followed by beast from Singerstrasse to Franzensplatz. Dr Steier's clinic children.
- Eberhardt returns with Marichi (Koellner's daughter, mother died of consumption). Lilli takes her; Lilli hugs father. Kaethe: "she can stay here till things get better." Tante Ilde: "She'll bring a blessing into the house, Leo."
- Eberhardt gives Marichi zwieback. Tante Ilde: "I'm coming every Thursday... Fanny sent word I was always to get enough."
- Carli dies (scream; Kaethe holds him to window). Night: "A child came in, a child went out." Irma: "charity was dangerous."

## VI. CORINNE
- Morning: Frau Stacher all love; Irma's malice. Irma: "Who's taking you tomorrow?" Tante Ilde: "Tomorrow I'm going to Fanny's." Irma: "I find it disgraceful" then asks Fanny to send Ferry to mountains. "Fanny's rich... only good business for women in Vienna." Tante Ilde: "Don't weep, Irma, we'll surely arrange about our Ferry."
- Fanny (Maria arranged) tells Tante Ilde Fanny wept at Carli's, bought white roses. Tante Ilde came to Kaethe's again; Fanny brought her home in taxi. Fanny: "I'd be better off dead."
- Lunch: restaurant **Zur Stadt Brunn** (Corinne, Tante Ilde). Pauli joins. Corinne upset at Fanny's. Pauli shocked ("Tante Ilde at Fanny's!").
- Half chicken each with rice; Arleberger wine (Budapest friend); "boiled beef" suggestion. Pauli gives banknotes ("presentli") beside chicken bones.
- Pauli's hand over Corinne's; turquoise ring. "Next year... tiny, tiny apartment." Pauli: "dress you in silver, Corinne."
- Tante Ilde, sickening, gives Pauli's money to poor woman with child in street ("Let them eat once"); "Vergelt's Gott."
- Irma at home: "What did Corinne give you to eat today?"

## VII. FANNY
- Fanny's flat: Empress Elisabeth, Franz Joseph, Franz Ferdinand & Hohenberg, Zita and children; Helleu etchings, Ingres "Source"; jewel elephants, rabbits, jade love-birds, amber canary; deep leather chairs, blue silk divan, blue carpet, cream porcelain stove. Father's house.
- Fanny's principle: "der Tag bringt's, der Tag nimmt's." Lunches at Bristol near door ("the head-waiter made no mistakes"). Blue gowns; black after Treaties of St. Germain and Trianon. Lover (the Count) and rival South American girl.
- Fanny: "Virtue, what is virtue?" Pauli: "Fanny, thanking the Lord God... Doxology." Fanny: "stupid ox."
- Family ledger: Fanny supports Kaethe, Irma's boys (boots, stockings), Maria's relatives; Anna hates her; Otto disdains; Mizzi admires.
- Maria and Fanny discuss Tante Ilde coming to Fanny's ("not done," "it's different").
- Saturday (Carli's funeral day): Tante Ilde weak, ill; gives carving to Irma; wears wrong skirt; leaves alcove curtains undrawn. Irma: "You won't lose the little figure?" Farewell embrace.
- Fanny's flat: Maria admits her; Tante Ilde in deep chair. Fanny's gifts: long black coat (fur-trimmed), gloves, leather bag (replacing "horror"). Forced fruit tree in blue ribbons.
- Lunch: oatmeal soup (milk), veal cutlet (Tante Ilde repulsed by white meat), Sacher tart, strong coffee with extra sugar.
- Ferry: Tante Ilde asks Fanny for knife; Fanny promises "six or eight blades" and country air. "Manny will tell us where."
- Fanny weeps, head on Tante Ilde's breast. Tante Ilde: "Fanny, precious one, you too, have some grief."
- Maria's gossip: Count to be lost; South American girl; Fanny's Hamur.
- Cemetery procession: Jacquingasse, Minoritenkirche, Carli's white box on Eberhardt's knees. Fanny's reflection in driver's coat glass. Café near cemetery: Fanny scolds stale semmels. Tante Ilde faints; Fanny takes her home by coach; Fanny gives Kaethe money.
- Upstairs: Maria undresses her; Tante Ilde mutters "alcove." Hermann arrives: "Pneumonia... she won't get through the night." Fanny sends for Capuchin monk. Monk anoints with Blessed Oils.
- Tante Ilde's last words: "Manny, dear, good Manny!" "Fanny, darling, you won't forget little Ferry?" Calls for Corinne (Corinne is with Pauli in restaurant, then Kaethe's). Dies.
- Funeral: Requiem at Capuchin Church; wreaths paid by Fanny (Mizzi's bill disputed). Lost bag at grave. Anna and Hermine attend church and cemetery. Liesel views body in Fanny's blue salon. Corinne watches two nights. Fanny's tears heal Kaethe. Final line: she "would soon be ... as if she had never been."
